name: IC 1613
tagline: A Local Group irregular whose Cepheid variable stars helped set the extragalactic distance scale.

facts.label: History
facts.value: Used by Baade to resolve stellar content

history: IC 1613 is an irregular galaxy on the Local Group's outskirts that holds a place in the history of distance measurement: Walter Baade used its Cepheid variable stars in the mid-20th century to help calibrate the extragalactic ladder. Gas-rich and only moderately clustered, it keeps making stars slowly — a control case for how a dwarf irregular ages without a big galaxy bullying it.
